claim: `service-watching` tells a persona that a service she answers for is broken. It launches exactly as the 49 other workstation units do, through one module under one pinned worktree, because every workstation service's start is composed from the same `RUNNER` constant and no page overrides it. So the alarm shares a single point of failure with every service it reports on: a fault in that path cannot take out some services and leave the alarm, it takes out the alarm and all of them together, which makes the alarm's own failure perfectly correlated with the largest outage it exists to report. Seen on 2026-09-12: `service-watching` was down 13.5 hours, 31 units are logged failing on that same path beside it, and its outage ledger recorded not one of them.

evidence:
The job. `service-watching.service-workstation.ts:7` defines it as 'the service telling a persona that a service she answers for is broken', and the rendered unit repeats that as its `Description`. `service-watching.module.code.ts:125` takes `healthFor(root)` over every workstation service, `:130` works out which persona champions the domain, and `carrying` at `:99` writes her a message. It is the fleet's alarm.

The shared path. Its unit at `/var/home/walton/.local/state/workstation-services/service-watching.service` reads `ExecStart=/usr/bin/env bash -c 'exec bun /var/home/walton/repos/akasha/.git/trees/service-workstation/infrastructure/service/workstation/modules/service-running/service-running.module.code.ts service-watching'`. All 50 `.service` files in that folder carry that same line, differing only in the trailing slug. That is not a per-page choice anyone made: `service-reading.module.code.ts:23` holds `RUNNER = "module/service-running"` and `:78` composes every workstation service's start from it, so the alarm gets the same launcher, out of the same pinned worktree, as the 49 services it reports on. Its page states no override; it is 14 lines and carries `slug`, `definition`, `enabled` and a `systemd` record.

What that means for correlation. A fault in that one shared path cannot break some services and spare the alarm. It breaks the alarm and all of them at once, so the alarm's own failure is perfectly correlated with the largest outage it exists to report. The bigger the outage, the likelier it is the one nobody is told about.

Seen. On 2026-09-12 `ff5b390b9e4` renamed the folder holding that launcher while the pinned worktree stayed at an earlier commit. `service-watching` last ran green at 18:02:04, then from 18:03:05 exited in milliseconds with `error: Module not found "/var/home/walton/repos/akasha/.git/trees/service-workstation/infrastructure/service/workstation/modules/service-running/service-running.module.code.ts"`, every minute until 07:33 the next morning. Thirty-one distinct units are logged failing on that same path across that window, `audit-running` and every `*-deploying` service among them, and all 50 named the same missing file.

What the alarm recorded for that outage: nothing. The ledger it keeps, `~/.local/state/workstation-services/service-outages.json` (`service-watching.module.code.ts:21`), today holds two entries, `model-account-upkeep-stall` and `eso-addon-deploying`, with `brokenSince` of 2026-09-13T14:00Z and 14:07Z — after recovery. Not one of the units that failed overnight has an entry, because the process that writes entries was one of them. No message went to a persona; the outage was diagnosed the next morning by a person.

How this differs from what is already filed. `a-folder-move-stops-the-service-whose-page-spells-the-moved-path` records the observation once, as an incident — `service-watching` out 25 hours, 'the alarm for this fault is the first thing this fault silences' — under the older mechanism where each service page spelled its own `runs` path as data and one stale string took one service down. That mechanism is gone; `runs` is now composed. What is here is the structural successor: not one page going stale, but one launch path shared by the watch and everything watched. `a-crash-looping-watch-service-reads-as-well-because-it-can-never-reach-failed` and `a-unit-that-fails-and-succeeds-within-a-timer-period-is-told-to-nobody` are about a healthy watcher misreading or mistiming its subjects; this is the watcher dying with them.
